newsitem.title: GERMANY: Heidelberger Druck sees '97 sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Heidelberger Druck sees '97 sales growth.

text.p: German printing machinery maker Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG said on Thursday it expected sales to top six billion marks in the current year, up from 5.1 billion marks in the year which ended on March 31.

Finance director Herbert Meyer told a news conference that the 1997/98 sales figure would include 870 million marks from the consolidated results of Linotype-Hell AG, which was taken over by Heidelberger last autumn.
Meyer also said he expected "moderate growth" in group earnings, although Linotype would lose around 50 million marks. Linotype should start earning profits by 2000, he said.
First quarter incoming orders were up 12 percent, thanks to one-off factors, while group sales posted a single-digit percentage rise, in line with plans, he said.
Heidelberger earlier announced 1996/97 group net profits up to 353 million marks from 268 million marks in the previous year.
The company, which is 57 percent owned by utility group RWE AG, plans to float 15 percent of its shares on the German stock market this year.
